title: RoutingPolicy
description: Which model answers a request, and what escalates to a more expensive one. Routing is a component with an explicit decision rule rather than a configuration constant, because no single model is optimal across all queries and budget constraints. A policy is part of the Configuration it belongs to -- configuration_id hashes it -- so a routed configuration is a different configuration and is measured as one, under the same EvalRun protocol as any other change.

method.description: fixed always uses tier 0, and exists so that a routed and an unrouted configuration take the same code path -- a policy bypassed for the common case is a policy whose common case is untested. cascade starts cheapest and escalates on a declared signal.

tiers.description: Cheapest first. The order IS the policy; nothing re-sorts it at run time.

family.description: Carried per tier so a routed run can still be checked against 'the judge is never the model under test'. Without it, escalating to the judge's own family would silently create the self-preference cycle judge-policy refuses.

escalate_on.description: gate-fail reuses the bounded control signal from the gate-feedback loop rather than inventing a second notion of 'not good enough'.

max_escalations.description: Required for cascade. The recorded hazard for a verification or retry loop is unbounded retry with no termination rule, which is why topology.max_iterations is required for a reflexive topology; an undeclared cap here is the same hazard by a different name.

then.description: A fixed policy may not declare escalation settings it can never use. Accepting and ignoring them is how router_policy_ref spent three versions as a field that existed and meant nothing; a configuration describing behaviour it does not have is worse than one describing none.
